sources.name: OGC GeoSPARQL - A Geographic Query Language for RDF Data 1.1
sources.role: feature/geometry identity, serialization, CRS and topological-relation contract
verified_facts: GeoSPARQL separates spatial Features from their Geometry resources and supports geometry serializations including WKT, GML, GeoJSON and KML.
Simple Features relation vocabulary and query functions include relations such as within, contains and overlaps.
Distance and geometric calculations are evaluated in the spatial reference system of the geometry, with measurement units made explicit where required.
semantic_limits: A GeoSPARQL relation assertion or query result is not proof that the geometry came from the exact HMLR authoritative polygon asset.
Geometry serialization, CRS identity, precision and source version must remain bound before any parcel containment result is accepted.
Optional entailment or inferred triples must not create a business row without explicit source evidence.

sources.name: OGC Features and Geometries JSON - Part 1: Core
sources.role: JSON-FG geometry/place, CRS, temporal and conformance-class contract
verified_facts: JSON-FG extends GeoJSON while conforming JSON-FG features and collections remain valid GeoJSON.
Mandatory extensions support coordinate reference systems beyond WGS 84 longitude/latitude, temporal feature characteristics and declared conformance classes.
When a geometry cannot be represented as valid GeoJSON geometry, JSON-FG encodes it using the place member.
semantic_limits: The geometry and place members must not be silently interchanged or reduced to a bounding box.
A coordRefSys declaration does not independently establish an ODN vertical datum, DTM semantics or source accuracy.
JSON-FG syntax and conformance do not prove exact HMLR containment or an authoritative numeric height.

sources.publisher: World Wide Web Consortium / Open Geospatial Consortium
sources.name: Spatial Data on the Web Best Practices
sources.role: spatial identifiers, CRS disclosure, versioning, metadata and Web publication best-practice contract
verified_facts: The document is an official W3C Working Group Note and OGC Best Practice, not an OGC Standard.
Publishers are advised to make the chosen coordinate reference system clear and to state how coordinate values are encoded.
Where positional accuracy and persistence over time are required, a static CRS or a measurement date accompanying coordinates is advised.
semantic_limits: Best-practice compliance, persistent URIs and metadata are not primary terrain measurement evidence.
Publishing a global CRS representation does not replace the native measurement CRS, vertical datum or transformation record.
Indexability, linking and metadata completeness do not prove exact parcel geometry or raster coverage.

sources.publisher: World Wide Web Consortium / Open Geospatial Consortium
sources.name: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.role: instant, interval, duration, temporal reference system and timezone contract
verified_facts: OWL-Time describes temporal properties using instants, intervals, durations and temporal ordering relations.
Time positions can use Gregorian time or another explicitly identified temporal reference system.
The inXSDDateTimeStamp property requires a timezone field for an instant.
semantic_limits: A timestamp or temporal ordering relation is not observation provenance, source accuracy or a height measurement.
Time-series modelling is outside OWL-Time's scope and requires additional domain modelling.
Measurement time, processing time and publication time must remain distinct and must not be inferred from one another.
